corpora.name: WideWorldImportersDW
corpora.about: Microsoft's data warehouse sample for WideWorldImporters, as an SSDT project read as `haruspex generate` reads a project: the procedures that load the warehouse from staging tables.

corpora.name: Northwind
corpora.about: Microsoft's Northwind sample, as its install script: a small order-processing database with a few reporting procedures.

corpora.name: pubs
corpora.about: Microsoft's pubs sample, as its install script: a small publishing database, the oldest of the samples.

corpora.name: JSON demos
corpora.about: The setup scripts of seven of Microsoft's JSON demonstration apps, each a small database of its own, read on its own and summed: procedures that build `FOR JSON` and read `OPENJSON`. Where an app comes in several copies, one for each web framework, one copy is taken.

corpora.name: ProfilesRNS

leftOut.why: Each defines a procedure that another script, whose name matches it, defines too; the procedure each file's own name promises is defined nowhere. Which definition an install keeps depends on the order the scripts run, so the figures read the script whose name matches.

corpora.about: ProfilesRNS, a research networking application for universities: one script per object, the largest corpus here, with `FOR JSON PATH`, XML methods, `OPENJSON`, dynamic SQL and schema names that contain dots. The upgrade scripts beside the schema are not taken.

corpora.name: Chinook
corpora.about: The Chinook music store sample, as Chris Woodruff's SSDT project: small create, read, update and delete procedures, many returning `SELECT *` as JSON. Its schema derives from Luis Rocha's Chinook database, also under MIT.

corpora.name: Ed-Fi OneRoster
corpora.about: The SQL Server scripts of the Ed-Fi Alliance's OneRoster API for one version of the standard: procedures that build JSON documents for an education data API.

corpora.name: Bitwarden
corpora.about: The database project of Bitwarden's server, a password manager: an SDK-style project and the largest real application here, with user-defined table types as parameters and JSON functions. Under the AGPL, so it is only ever fetched, never vendored.

corpora.name: tSQLt

leftOut.why: A file of a test run's output, committed beside the scripts. It creates the framework's objects a second time, so read with the others it makes each of them an object defined twice.

corpora.about: tSQLt, a unit-testing framework for T-SQL: the scripts of its SDK-style project, read as a folder, since the project takes every script below it, the test output among them. Dynamic SQL throughout, CLR procedures and `sql_variant`.

corpora.name: First Responder Kit
corpora.about: Brent Ozar's First Responder Kit, one install script per procedure: dynamic SQL, dynamic management views, temporary tables and `FOR XML`. The script that installs them all at once repeats the others and is not taken.

corpora.name: Ola Hallengren's Maintenance Solution
corpora.about: Ola Hallengren's SQL Server Maintenance Solution, as its install script: the most widely deployed maintenance procedures, built on dynamic SQL and system views.
